airport.name: Wichita Falls Municipal Airport / Sheppard Air Force Base

summary: Wichita Falls Municipal Airport (SPS) is a joint-use airfield sharing its runways and facilities with Sheppard Air Force Base in north Texas, just south of the Oklahoma border. The base is best known as the home of the 82nd Training Wing and the prestigious Euro-NATO Joint Jet Pilot Training (ENJJPT) program, one of the most selective pilot training pipelines in the U.S. Air Force. The civilian terminal provides commercial service to the Wichita Falls metropolitan area while military operations dominate overall flight activity.
faqs:
Q: Is Wichita Falls Airport shared with a military base?
A: Yes, the airfield is jointly operated with Sheppard Air Force Base, which trains thousands of U.S. and allied military personnel annually.

Q: Does the airport offer commercial passenger flights?
A: Yes, the civilian side provides limited scheduled commercial service, though many travelers drive to nearby DFW or Lawton for more flight options.

Q: What is the Euro-NATO Joint Jet Pilot Training program?
A: ENJJPT is an elite multinational pilot training program hosted at Sheppard AFB, producing fighter and bomber pilots for the U.S. Air Force and several NATO allies.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Wichita Falls?
A: The airport is approximately 5 miles north of the city center, a short 10-15 minute drive via US-287.
transport_tips: Rental cars are the most convenient option for getting to and from SPS, as public transit is limited. Taxis and rideshare services can be requested but availability may be sporadic, so booking ahead is recommended. The airport is directly accessible from US-287 and US-82, making it an easy drive from most parts of north Texas and southern Oklahoma.
local_tip: If you're visiting the area, plan your trip around a Sheppard AFB air show if possible — the base occasionally hosts open-house events featuring demonstrations by the very student pilots training on-site.
